summary: Turn 23. Final source step for the active Candidate 0922502bc12a4af68ee74cb77942fd72 at the run's time boundary; the confirmed finding is unchanged (CLM-DURABLE-BAL, outcome violated, confirmed true) and the durability candidate remains paused with its unit disposed. This turn narrows the even-N quorum question to its actual precondition: a recovery that rebuilds from a non-majority slow quorum can only conflict with an existing decision if the recovering replica reached the recovery path without holding the committed value. handleCommit records COMMITTED with the committed command for every receiver, and startRecoveryForInstance returns early when inst.Status >= COMMITTED and inst.Cmds != nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1135), so a replica that got the Commit cannot be the one that restarts the instance; and because bcastCommit skips peers with !r.Alive (epaxos/epaxos.go:579-600) while crtInstance advances only together with creating an instance entry, the required missing-Commit state is a membership/liveness condition (A4) rather than a consequence of the quorum sizes alone. Submitted action=research with feedback referencing the candidate, B-COMMIT, B-RECOVERY-START, B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER and F-COMMITTED, stating the narrowed precondition and explicitly declining to claim a defect or create a new obligation at the boundary. Remaining keeps the frontier intact: whether membership/liveness handling can produce the missing-Commit state (A4 unread), whether the Accept phase's majority requirement already prevents a conflicting commit in every recovery branch including restart-with-NOOP, whether N parity is enforced outside the captured files, and that the confirmed durable-metadata violation still lacks a demonstrated consequence because no record reader exists in the captured source. Preflight validation returns valid=true; acceptance remains the controller's.
